abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Robo‐advice has the potential to provide affordable financial advice to assist older adults with building and managing retirement income. Yet robo‐advice uptake among those aged 60 to 80 years is low, and little is known about how they engage with robo‐advice. Our study examines the drivers and barriers to robo‐advice access and adoption among older adults, and provides practical recommendations for industry and policymakers. Drawing on qualitative surveys and interviews with academic and industry experts familiar with the Australian financial advice landscape. We identify six core themes and their possible interrelationships, which likely affect older adults' access and adoption: robo‐advice design, digital and financial capabilities, trust, psychological comfort, regulatory deficiencies, and social influence. In integrating our findings with the technology acceptance and financial planning literature, we construct a conceptual framework that responds to calls for more comprehensive explanations of consumer behavior toward robo‐advice.

ur.tldr: 通过老年人调查及行业专家访谈，梳理其采用智能投顾的障碍，包括系统设计、数字与金融能力、信任、心理舒适度、监管不足和社会影响，并据此构建消费采纳框架与实践建议。

title:
